decisions.reason: The existing BOM modification includes the solenoid mechanism and custom spout but omits the station-button control circuit required by the approved dispensing approach.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Go ahead with that approach, and please match the rendering as closely as possible; I really like both its appearance and functionality. I do want one change from the rendering: move the plate labeled "Elena's Chai Whisk" from the back of the machine to the front. The spout and mixers will face the baristas, while customers will view the machine from another angle, so the "Elena's Chai Whisk" plate needs to face the customer.

value_updates.spout_component_selection: custom-fabricated stainless-steel spout matching the supplied rendering as closely as possible

decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message modification recording the approved solenoid valve and press-to-open, release-to-stop station-button behavior.
The candidate already records the approved gravity-fed solenoid dispensing path and absence of retained matcha in the spout or tubing; its existing pour-quality constraints remain unchanged.
Approval of specific dispensing-control wiring does not change the requirement to deliver a system layout, and no candidate attribute is made obsolete.
The approved solenoid control does not alter the requirement that the bowl seal prevent liquid from reaching electronics.
The dispensing-control decision does not change or remove the existing leak-containment requirement.
The candidate already has same-message events resolving the earlier scope uncertainty and recording the custom stainless-steel, rendering-matched spout.
The approved dispensing-control circuit does not change the selected 120V wall-power source or the deferral of battery power.
The source confirms that the spout faces the baristas, which is already the candidate's current orientation and therefore requires no state change.
The dispensing-control wiring decision does not modify the structural support or operational-stability constraints.
The approved solenoid dispensing control does not change the requirement to minimize splashing during mixing.
The approved dispensing approach does not replace or narrow the existing requirement that the spout remain removable or easy to flush and clean.
